questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. What current in Amperes flows through the resistor?
Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance in Ohms?
A 100 W bulb operates on a 200 V line. What is the current drawn by the bulb in Amperes?
A transformer steps down 240 V to 12 V. If the primary has 1000 turns, how many turns are on the secondary coil?
A 1000 W room heater runs for 5 hours. How many kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electrical energy are consumed?
questions.explanation: Energy = 1 kW × 5 h = 5 kWh.

questions.question: What fundamental law of physics ensures that the polarity of induced EMF opposes the magnetic flux change producing it?
questions.explanation: Lenz's law is a consequence of the conservation of energy; otherwise, induced current would create unbounded kinetic energy without doing mechanical work.

questions.question: Which safety component in a three-pin plug is made longest and thickest to ensure it connects first and disconnects last?
questions.explanation: The earth pin is physically longer so the metal casing of the appliance is grounded before live electrical contact is established, protecting users against shock.

questions.question: What type of electrical current is produced by a rotating coil connected to a pair of continuous slip rings?
questions.explanation: Slip rings maintain continuous contact with coil terminals, preserving the sinusoidal alternating polarity of induced EMF to output AC.

questions.question: If the temperature of an intrinsic semiconductor such as silicon is raised, does its electrical resistance increase or decrease?
questions.explanation: Unlike metals, semiconductors have a negative temperature coefficient of resistance; heat frees electron-hole pairs across the bandgap, lowering resistance.

questions.question: What parasitic circulating currents in a solid transformer iron core are minimized by laminating the core?
questions.explanation: Alternating magnetic flux induces circulating loops of current known as eddy currents in bulk iron, which are minimized by thin insulated laminations.

questions.question: Two point charges of +8 μC and -2 μC are placed 0.2 m apart. What is the magnitude and nature of the electrostatic force between them? (k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
options: 3.6 N attractive
3.6 N repulsive
0.36 N attractive
7.2 N repulsive

questions.question: An electric toaster operates at 220 V and draws 5 A. What is the electrical resistance of the toaster heating element?
A cylindrical wire of length L and resistance 10 Ω is drawn through a die so that its radius is halved while volume is conserved. What is its new resistance?
questions.explanation: When radius halves, cross-sectional area drops to A/4. Volume conservation requires length to become 4L. New resistance R' = ρ(4L)/(A/4) = 16(ρL/A) = 16 × 10 = 160 Ω.

questions.question: In the circuit shown, three 9 Ω resistors are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery with an internal resistance of 1 Ω. What is the terminal voltage of the battery?
options: 9 V
8 V
questions.explanation: Equivalent external resistance R_p = 9 / 3 = 3 Ω. Total resistance R_total = 3 + 1 = 4 Ω. Circuit current I = 12 / 4 = 3 A. Terminal voltage V = I × R_p = 3 A × 3 Ω = 9 V.

questions.question: How many 176 Ω resistors connected in parallel are required to draw a current of 5 A from a 220 V supply line?
questions.explanation: Desired equivalent resistance R_p = V / I = 220 / 5 = 44 Ω. Since R_p = R / n → 44 = 176 / n → n = 176 / 44 = 4.

questions.question: A domestic electricity meter records a consumption of 250 units in a month. If the utility company charges 7.5 Taka per unit plus a fixed meter rent of 50 Taka, what is the total electricity bill?
options: 1925 Taka
1875 Taka
2000 Taka
1825 Taka
questions.explanation: Energy charge = 250 units × 7.5 Taka/unit = 1875 Taka. Total bill = 1875 + 50 (meter rent) = 1925 Taka.

questions.question: A step-up transformer with 95% efficiency delivers 19 kW of electrical power at 2000 V. What is the electric current flowing into the primary coil if it is supplied at 200 V?
questions.explanation: Output power P_out = 19,000 W. Efficiency η = P_out / P_in → 0.95 = 19,000 / P_in → P_in = 20,000 W. Primary current I_p = P_in / V_p = 20,000 W ÷ 200 V = 100 A.

questions.question: A 2.0 m long horizontal wire carries a current of 10 A from west to east in a region where the Earth's magnetic field is 5 × 10⁻⁵ T pointing horizontally north. What is the magnetic force on the wire?
options: 1.0 × 10⁻³ N vertically upward
1.0 × 10⁻³ N vertically downward
2.5 × 10⁻⁴ N south
Zero
questions.explanation: F = BIL = (5 × 10⁻⁵ T) × (10 A) × (2.0 m) = 1.0 × 10⁻³ N. By Fleming's Left-Hand Rule (Field North, Current East), the force points vertically upward.

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitance 50 μF is charged to a potential difference of 200 V. What is the total electric charge stored on each plate?
questions.explanation: Q = C × V = (50 × 10⁻⁶ F) × 200 V = 0.01 Coulombs.

questions.question: Two resistors of 20 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in parallel across a 60 V DC line. What is the ratio of electric power consumed by the 20 Ω resistor to that by the 30 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: In parallel, both have the same voltage V = 60 V. P = V² / R. P1 / P2 = R2 / R1 = 30 / 20 = 3/2.

questions.question: A coil of 200 turns and cross-sectional area 0.05 m² is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.4 T. If the coil is flipped by 180° in 0.1 s, what average EMF is induced?
questions.explanation: Initial flux per turn Φ1 = BA = 0.4 × 0.05 = 0.02 Wb. When flipped 180°, Φ2 = -0.02 Wb. ΔΦ = 0.04 Wb. Induced EMF e = N(ΔΦ / Δt) = 200 × (0.04 / 0.1) = 200 × 0.4 = 80 V.

questions.question: An electric tea kettle rated 220 V, 1100 W takes 4 minutes to bring water to boil. How many Coulombs of charge passed through the heating element?
options: 5 C

questions.question: A 12 V battery supplies 2 A of current to a circuit for 1 hour. What is the total chemical energy transformed by the battery?
questions.explanation: Energy W = V × I × t = 12 V × 2 A × 3600 s = 86,400 Joules.

questions.question: A silver wire has a resistance of 2.1 Ω at 20°C. If the temperature coefficient of resistance of silver is 0.004 °C⁻¹, what will its resistance be at 100°C?
A power station generates 50 MW of electricity at 10 kV. Before long-distance transmission, the voltage is stepped up to 250 kV. What is the transmission line current?
Three identical capacitors of 9 μF each are connected in series. What is the equivalent capacitance of the combination?
options: 3 μF
27 μF
1 μF
6 μF
questions.explanation: For n identical capacitors in series, C_s = C / n = 9 μF / 3 = 3 μF.

questions.question: Why does an aluminum ring jump upward into the air when an alternating current is suddenly switched on through an underlying solenoid?
options: Rising magnetic flux induces an opposing magnetic field in the ring, causing mutual magnetic repulsion (Lenz's Law)
The solenoid attracts gravitational waves that lift the ring
Aluminum becomes permanently magnetized as a south pole
The alternating current electrostatically charges the air below the ring
questions.correct_answer: Rising magnetic flux induces an opposing magnetic field in the ring, causing mutual magnetic repulsion (Lenz's Law)
questions.explanation: When current turns on, upward flux increases. By Lenz's law, the induced current in the ring produces a downward opposing magnetic field. The like poles repel, thrusting the ring into the air.

questions.question: A homeowner connects a 100 W bulb and a 40 W bulb in series across a 220 V line. Which bulb glows brighter and why?
options: The 40 W bulb glows brighter because its higher resistance dissipates more power with the same series current
The 100 W bulb glows brighter because it has a higher rated wattage
Both bulbs glow with equal brightness because the current is identical
Neither bulb glows because series connection blocks current
questions.correct_answer: The 40 W bulb glows brighter because its higher resistance dissipates more power with the same series current
questions.explanation: Rated R = V²/P, so R_40W > R_100W. In series, both share the same current I. Since P_dissipated = I²R, the 40 W bulb dissipates more power and glows noticeably brighter.

questions.question: What happens to the reading of an ammeter and a voltmeter if they are accidentally swapped in a circuit (voltmeter in series, ammeter in parallel with the load)?
options: The voltmeter's huge resistance reduces circuit current to near zero, while the ammeter risks burning out from drawing heavy current
Both instruments function normally without error
The voltmeter explodes instantly while the ammeter reads zero
The power supply converts from DC to AC automatically
questions.correct_answer: The voltmeter's huge resistance reduces circuit current to near zero, while the ammeter risks burning out from drawing heavy current
questions.explanation: A voltmeter has megaohm internal resistance; placing it in series chokes circuit current to microamperes. An ammeter has near-zero resistance; placing it across the load creates a short circuit that can burn the meter.

questions.question: Why does touching an ungrounded appliance with wet hands present a much higher electrocution risk than with dry skin?
options: Water and dissolved skin salts reduce human electrical contact resistance from over 100,000 Ω down to less than 1,000 Ω
Wet hands attract electrical charges from the air like a lightning rod
Water accelerates the speed of light in the nervous system
Dry skin has zero resistance while wet skin is a superconductor
questions.correct_answer: Water and dissolved skin salts reduce human electrical contact resistance from over 100,000 Ω down to less than 1,000 Ω
questions.explanation: Dry stratum corneum provides high resistance (~100 kΩ). Moisture containing dissolved electrolytes penetrates skin pores, dropping body resistance below 1 kΩ and allowing lethal currents (>30 mA) to flow at 220 V.

questions.question: Why are copper coils wound on an iron armature in electric motors, rather than winding them in empty space?
options: Iron has high magnetic permeability, concentrating and amplifying the magnetic flux through the coils
Iron prevents copper wire from conducting electric current
Iron insulates the motor against electrical short circuits
Empty space repels all magnetic fields
questions.correct_answer: Iron has high magnetic permeability, concentrating and amplifying the magnetic flux through the coils
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic iron provides a low-reluctance path that channels and multiplies magnetic flux density hundreds of times, dramatically increasing motor torque (Torque ∝ B).

questions.question: A technician connects an ideal voltmeter across the terminals of an open-circuit battery and measures 1.5 V. When a 5 Ω resistor is connected, the voltmeter reads 1.25 V. What is the internal resistance of the battery?
questions.explanation: EMF E = 1.5 V. Terminal V = 1.25 V. Current I = V / R = 1.25 / 5 = 0.25 A. Voltage drop Ir = E - V = 1.5 - 1.25 = 0.25 V. Internal resistance r = 0.25 V / 0.25 A = 1.0 Ω.

questions.question: Why does a compass needle placed above a wire carrying current from South to North deflect toward the West? (SNOW rule)
options: By Ampere's Right-Hand Grip Rule, circular magnetic field lines run from East to West above the conductor
The Earth's geographic North Pole attracts the wire's electrons westward
Current pushes air molecules toward the west
The compass needle becomes positively charged and repels the battery
questions.correct_answer: By Ampere's Right-Hand Grip Rule, circular magnetic field lines run from East to West above the conductor
questions.explanation: Pointing the right thumb North, curled fingers point West above the wire. The North-seeking pole of the compass aligns along this circular field line, deflecting West (SNOW: South to North Over West).

questions.question: Why do high-voltage transmission towers feature three or four bundles of spaced conductor wires for each phase rather than a single thick wire?
options: Bundling increases effective cross-sectional radius, reducing electric field strength at the surface to suppress corona discharge
Multiple wires allow separate frequencies to travel independently
Bundled wires make it easier for birds to perch safely
It is impossible to manufacture copper wires thicker than 1 cm
questions.correct_answer: Bundling increases effective cross-sectional radius, reducing electric field strength at the surface to suppress corona discharge
questions.explanation: A bundle behaves as a single conductor of large equivalent diameter. This lowers the surface electric field intensity below the dielectric breakdown of air (30 kV/cm), suppressing power loss and buzzing from corona discharge.

questions.question: How does a Residual Current Circuit Breaker (RCCB) detect an electrical leakage fault in a domestic installation?
options: It monitors whether the current leaving through the live wire exactly equals the current returning through the neutral wire
It measures the overall temperature of the copper cables
It counts the number of appliances switched on in the house
It monitors the frequency of alternating current from the power station
questions.correct_answer: It monitors whether the current leaving through the live wire exactly equals the current returning through the neutral wire
questions.explanation: In a healthy circuit, I_live = I_neutral. If a human touches a live wire or insulation leaks to earth, I_live ≠ I_neutral. The differential current transformer detects this imbalance and trips the breaker within milliseconds.

questions.question: Why does a capacitor block direct current (DC) in steady state while allowing alternating current (AC) to pass continuously?
options: In DC, the dielectric charges fully and opposing electric field balances source voltage; in AC, continuous reversal alternates charging and discharging
Capacitors melt under DC voltage but freeze under AC voltage
DC current is absorbed into the aluminum foil plates as heat
AC electrons physically tunnel across the dielectric gap without resistance
questions.correct_answer: In DC, the dielectric charges fully and opposing electric field balances source voltage; in AC, continuous reversal alternates charging and discharging
questions.explanation: Under DC, once Q = CV is reached, no further charge flows (I = 0, capacitive reactance Xc = 1/(2πfC) → ∞ as f → 0). AC continuously alternates polarities, driving continuous displacement current through the circuit.

questions.question: What is the reason that a piece of unmagnetized iron is attracted to both the North pole and the South pole of a permanent magnet?
options: Magnetic induction causes atomic domains in the iron to reorient, always presenting an opposite attracting pole to the approaching magnet
Iron atoms contain only positive magnetic monopoles
Permanent magnets create static electric charges on iron
The Earth's gravity pulls the iron toward magnetic materials
questions.correct_answer: Magnetic induction causes atomic domains in the iron to reorient, always presenting an opposite attracting pole to the approaching magnet
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic domains readily align with external magnetic fields. Near a North pole, the iron develops an induced South pole facing it; near a South pole, it develops an induced North pole. Both yield attraction.

questions.question: Why does the efficiency of a practical transformer never reach 100%?
options: Energy is lost due to copper winding resistance (I²R), core hysteresis, eddy currents, and magnetic flux leakage
Transformers violate Ohm's law
Electrons are absorbed by the secondary turns
The iron core radiates nuclear energy
questions.correct_answer: Energy is lost due to copper winding resistance (I²R), core hysteresis, eddy currents, and magnetic flux leakage
questions.explanation: Real transformers suffer from Joule heating in copper windings, magnetic domain friction (hysteresis loss), induced eddy currents in the core, and imperfect inductive coupling between coils.

questions.question: Why is the neutral wire in a domestic electrical distribution system grounded at the local distribution transformer?
options: To establish a stable zero-volt reference potential and prevent dangerous voltage floating during phase imbalances
To double the current delivered to consumer homes
To eliminate the need for an earth wire in domestic appliances
To return all electric power back to the coal power plant
questions.correct_answer: To establish a stable zero-volt reference potential and prevent dangerous voltage floating during phase imbalances
questions.explanation: Grounding the neutral at the substation anchors the neutral point to 0 V relative to Earth, preventing neutral float and ensuring balanced 220 V phase-to-neutral voltages across all consumers.

questions.question: Why do two parallel wires carrying currents in the SAME direction attract each other, while currents in OPPOSITE directions repel?
options: Magnetic fields between like currents partially cancel, creating net inward Lorentz forces; opposing currents concentrate field between them, pushing wires apart
Like currents have opposite electrostatic charges
Parallel wires experience gravitational attraction
Wires carrying current in the same direction share the same electrons
questions.correct_answer: Magnetic fields between like currents partially cancel, creating net inward Lorentz forces; opposing currents concentrate field between them, pushing wires apart
questions.explanation: By the Right-Hand Rule and F = I(L × B), parallel currents experience attractive Lorentz forces (F/L = μ₀I1I2 / 2πd), while antiparallel currents experience repulsive forces.

questions.question: A student builds a simple DC motor but forgets to include the split-ring commutator, using solid slip rings instead. What will the motor armature do when connected to a DC battery?
options: It will rotate a quarter or half turn and then oscillate back and forth around equilibrium without continuously spinning
It will spin twice as fast in the clockwise direction
It will immediately explode due to overcurrent
It will transform into an alternating current generator
questions.correct_answer: It will rotate a quarter or half turn and then oscillate back and forth around equilibrium without continuously spinning
questions.explanation: Without a commutator reversing current every 180°, torque reverses once the coil overshoots the neutral plane, pulling it backward and causing it to halt at magnetic alignment.

questions.question: In a bridge rectifier circuit made of four diodes, what is the key operational advantage over a center-tapped transformer with two diodes?
options: It utilizes the entire transformer secondary winding on both AC half-cycles without requiring a bulky center-tapped transformer
It produces pure DC without requiring any smoothing capacitors
It doubles the incoming AC frequency to 100 kHz
It eliminates all heat dissipation completely
questions.correct_answer: It utilizes the entire transformer secondary winding on both AC half-cycles without requiring a bulky center-tapped transformer
questions.explanation: A bridge rectifier achieves full-wave rectification using an ordinary two-terminal secondary winding, delivering higher transformer utilization factor and lower peak inverse voltage per diode.

questions.question: Why does an ammeter read a non-zero current when an AC voltage is applied across an ideal capacitor, even though the space between its plates is a non-conductive insulator?
options: The time-varying electric field between the plates constitutes Maxwell's displacement current, which equals conduction current in the external wires
Electrons spark physically across the dielectric vacuum
Capacitor plates act as miniature alternating current batteries
Air molecules between the plates undergo continuous nuclear fusion
questions.correct_answer: The time-varying electric field between the plates constitutes Maxwell's displacement current, which equals conduction current in the external wires
questions.explanation: As AC voltage oscillates, electric flux between plates changes (dΦ_E/dt ≠ 0). This changing electric field generates a displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) that maintains circuit continuity.

questions.question: Why does adding more branches in parallel to a household distribution board cause the total main current to increase?
options: Each new parallel branch provides an extra path for current, increasing total current drawn from the mains (I_total = I1 + I2 + ...)
The supply voltage automatically rises to power the new branch
Parallel connections increase the total circuit resistance
Adding appliances causes the electric meter to spin backward
questions.correct_answer: Each new parallel branch provides an extra path for current, increasing total current drawn from the mains (I_total = I1 + I2 + ...)
questions.explanation: By Kirchhoff's Current Law, the total current entering a junction equals the sum of branch currents. Since each branch draws I_k = V/R_k independently at 220 V, total current increases with every active load.

questions.question: What is the reason why magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops with no beginning or end, whereas electrostatic field lines begin on positive charges and terminate on negative charges?
options: Isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature, whereas isolated electric charges exist
Magnetic fields have zero energy
Electric charges cannot move, while magnetic poles move continuously
Magnetic field lines are made of physical iron filaments
questions.correct_answer: Isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature, whereas isolated electric charges exist
questions.explanation: Gauss's law for magnetism (∇·B = 0) confirms that magnetic monopoles do not exist. Cutting a magnet in half creates new pairs of poles, so field lines must always form continuous closed loops.

questions.question: Why does a miniature circuit breaker (MCB) provide superior protection over a traditional rewirable porcelain wire fuse?
options: MCB trips rapidly and precisely via magnetic and bimetallic mechanisms, and can be reset with a switch without handling live wires
MCBs never trip even during a severe short circuit
MCBs reduce monthly electricity bills by 50%
MCBs convert 220 V AC electricity into battery DC power
questions.correct_answer: MCB trips rapidly and precisely via magnetic and bimetallic mechanisms, and can be reset with a switch without handling live wires
questions.explanation: An MCB combines thermal overload protection (bimetallic strip) and instantaneous magnetic short-circuit protection (solenoid trip). It is safer, reusable, and eliminates the hazard of incorrect fuse wire sizing.

questions.question: How does a moving-coil galvanometer achieve a linear, evenly spaced scale for current deflection?
options: Cylindrical soft-iron core and curved pole pieces produce a radial magnetic field, ensuring deflecting torque is strictly proportional to current
The restoring spring has a non-linear spring constant
The pointer is equipped with a digital optical lens
The coil moves in a completely non-magnetic environment
questions.correct_answer: Cylindrical soft-iron core and curved pole pieces produce a radial magnetic field, ensuring deflecting torque is strictly proportional to current
questions.explanation: A radial magnetic field ensures the coil plane is always parallel to field lines (sin θ = 1). Deflecting torque τ = NIAB is directly proportional to current I, balancing linear spring torque kθ to give θ ∝ I.

questions.question: In a series circuit containing two different incandescent lamps, why does unscrewing one lamp immediately extinguish the other lamp as well?
options: A series circuit has only a single continuous loop; removing one component creates an open circuit that stops all current
The remaining lamp is overwhelmed by excess voltage and burns out
The second lamp's resistance drops to zero
Current flows backward into the electric meter
questions.correct_answer: A series circuit has only a single continuous loop; removing one component creates an open circuit that stops all current
questions.explanation: In series, all components share the same unbroken path. Removing any element breaks the circuit loop (R → ∞), reducing current to zero throughout the entire circuit.

questions.question: Why does electrostatic induction cause an uncharged metal sphere placed near a positive charge to experience net attraction rather than repulsion?
options: Induced negative charges on the near side are closer to the external charge than induced positive charges on the far side
The metal sphere destroys the external electric field
Positive charges in the sphere turn negative automatically
The sphere is pulled exclusively by Earth's gravity
questions.correct_answer: Induced negative charges on the near side are closer to the external charge than induced positive charges on the far side
questions.explanation: By Coulomb's law F ∝ 1/r², the attractive force on the nearer induced negative charges is strictly greater than the repulsive force on the farther induced positive charges, yielding net attraction.

questions.question: Why does a transformer core hum with a low acoustic buzz (typically 100 Hz or 120 Hz) during operation?
options: Magnetostriction causes the ferromagnetic core laminations to physically expand and contract twice per AC cycle
Electrons vibrate against the air molecules outside the casing
The copper coils are rattling against loose terminal screws
The electric current undergoes nuclear resonance in the insulation
questions.correct_answer: Magnetostriction causes the ferromagnetic core laminations to physically expand and contract twice per AC cycle
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials experience microscopic mechanical strain (magnetostriction) when magnetized. Because elongation occurs twice every AC cycle regardless of field polarity, 50 Hz AC drives 100 Hz acoustic vibrations.
